findings.source_passage: "I think you've given him too much, Tommy," said Tuppence innocently. "I fancy he wants to give some of it back." It was possibly this remark which induced the driver to move on.
findings.source_locator: Opening paragraphs, narrator's dry aside after Tuppence's line
findings.why_it_matters: Christie's deadpan narratorial comment ('It was possibly this remark which induced the driver to move on') is a signature piece of free-indirect irony; the draft preserves the dialogue but drops the narrator's wry gloss, losing the voice beat entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the narrator's aside verbatim: 'It was possibly this remark which induced the driver to move away.' It is two short clauses and costs nothing in compression.

findings.source_passage: "That's the curious part about speaking the truth. No one does believe it. I found that out this morning."
findings.source_locator: After the taxi argument, before the restaurant suggestion
findings.why_it_matters: This is the segment's most aphoristic, thematically charged line—Tuppence's ironic epistemology about truth-telling underpins the imposture plot. The draft preserves the words but immediately pivots ('Now—lunch'), cutting the Savoy/Ritz/Piccadilly comic exchange that gives the aphorism its breathing room and makes it land. The compression into a blunt pivot erases the comic rhythm that makes the line a signature.
findings.suggested_fix: After the truth-aphorism, restore at least the quick Savoy/Ritz exchange so the line has the comedic pause Christie gave it before Tuppence's practical pivot to lunch.

findings.source_passage: "Is this a new brand of humour? Or is your brain really unhinged?" inquired Tommy.
findings.why_it_matters: The draft collapses this to 'Is your brain unhinged?'—cutting the first half ('new brand of humour') and the narratorial tag 'inquired Tommy.' The two-part question is distinctively Christie: the first clause politely entertains one possibility before the sharper second; dropping it flattens Tommy's register.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full two-clause question verbatim: 'Is this a new brand of humour? Or is your brain really unhinged?'

findings.source_passage: "And people say that coincidences don't happen!" Tuppence tackled her Pêche Melba happily.
findings.source_locator: After Tommy confirms he saw Whittington near Lyons'
findings.why_it_matters: This one-line coda to the Jane Finn coincidence revelation is a neat thematic marker—Christie ironically endorsing coincidence as plot engine at the very moment the story depends on one. The draft omits both the exclamation and the happy action beat entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert after Tommy's 'I didn't notice him particularly' line: '"And people say that coincidences don't happen!" Tuppence tackled her Pêche Melba happily.' It takes one line.

findings.source_passage: "Oh, anyway, it will be rather a lark. What are you doing this afternoon?" "Well," said Tuppence meditatively. "I _had_ thought of hats! Or perhaps silk stockings! Or perhaps----" "Hold hard," admonished Tommy. "There's a limit to fifty pounds!"
findings.source_locator: After the sleuthing plan is agreed, before 'The day passed pleasantly'
findings.why_it_matters: This short comic exchange (hats, silk stockings, Tommy's 'Hold hard') characterises Tuppence's gleeful spending impulse and Tommy's mild prudence—exactly the dynamic the book builds on. The draft jumps straight to 'Dinner and a show tonight?' collapsing two distinct comic beats into one.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert a brief version of the afternoon shopping discussion before the dinner-and-show agreement to preserve both character beats.

findings.source_passage: The day passed pleasantly. The evening even more so. Two of the five-pound notes were now irretrievably dead.
findings.source_locator: Transitional paragraph between planning lunch and next-morning action
findings.why_it_matters: 'Irretrievably dead' is a miniature Christie comic epitaph with its own rhythm. The draft replaces it with 'Two of the five-pound notes died gallantly'—a paraphrase that changes the register from Christie's dry understatement to slightly heroic mock-elegy, losing the original's tone.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore: 'The day passed pleasantly. The evening even more so. Two of the five-pound notes were now irretrievably dead.'

summary: Three medium-severity findings (narratorial ironic aside erased, comic two-part exchange flattened, thematic coincidence line absent) plus two low-severity losses cumulatively flatten Christie's register across the chapter; the three mediums alone trigger regeneration.
